scope: A source-bound, deterministic, local derivative-order comparison between OpenAI manuscript Lemma 8.6 equation (8.19) and the hypotheses of norm_derivativeWord_inverse_le at one pinned source commit.
required_inputs: OpenAI manuscript PDF with the locked byte count and SHA-256
Pinned Lean source file with the locked byte count and SHA-256
detector_excluded_inputs: Independent mathematical review or its conclusions
Any unpinned or later repository content
checked_relation: If the manuscript's displayed estimate requires input order m+k and both named Lean hypotheses require xJet (w.length+j), the local comparison reports an order gap when j>k. A missing, ambiguous, or contradictory extraction is unresolved, not aligned.
interpretation_limitations: The Lean declaration is a derivative-word statement; rewriting it as a C_y^m estimate involves additional mathematical interpretation that this detector does not certify.
A stronger Lean hypothesis does not prove the stronger manuscript estimate false or the final Navier-Stokes result false.
Matching derivative orders alone would not establish equality of objects, definitions, quantifiers, domains, or all hypotheses.
A successful Lean build, if later obtained, would establish kernel acceptance of formalized declarations, not manuscript or Clay statement identity.
This candidate diagnostic cannot issue or mutate QualificationReceipts, CurrentUseBindings, AuthorizationGrants, or execution authority.
failure_behavior: Absent, ambiguous, altered, oversized, or unparseable source bytes fail closed without a positive alignment verdict.
